articles.headline: Week 9 betting preview: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
articles.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 9 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
articles.headlineJa: 第9週ベッティングプレビュー：日曜日の分析、おすすめの賭け、TD予想
articles.descriptionJa: 専門家が第9週のオッズとプレイヤープロップスを深く分析し、ベッティングのヒントとおすすめのプレーを提案します。
articles.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: Find betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 9.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Jump to:

Bowen's favorite bets

Solak's plays | Walder's props

Clay's TD projections

Bowen's favorite bets

Heading into the Week 9 Sunday slate, I'm going to start with the late-window Packers-Patriots matchup in New England, giving you my pick for the game. I have some thoughts there on the Green Bay defense based on what it is showing on the tape. Plus, I have a couple more game picks to look at -- including a two-team teaser -- and I'll throw down some props, too.

Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots

4:25 p.m. ET on Fox; Line: NE -3.5, O/U: 45.5

I'll start with the Packers' defense under coordinator Jonathan Gannon. This unit is playing its best football of the season, allowing 14.8 PPG over the past four while giving up just 4.5 yards per play. The Packers are taking the ball away, too, recording 11 turnovers in this four-game stretch. We'll see a lot of late movement in the secondary, with multiple fronts and disguised pressures, which will force Patriots quarterback Drake Maye to read it out post-snap with a wide receiver group that is still banged up. Offensively for the Packers, the combo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden creates vertical opportunities for quarterback Jordan Love. My concern here? Can Green Bay get the running game going with Josh Jacobs? I don't see a burst yet from Jacobs, which the Packers will need to attack the edges on outside zone run concepts. But with the added prep time, I like Green Bay to cover here.

Denver Broncos -2.5 at Carolina Panthers

The Panthers' offensive line is beat up, and they can't protect consistently on the edges, as quarterback Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times over the last two games. That's trouble versus a Denver pass rush that has a pressure rate of 40.4% (second highest in the league). Yes, Jonah Coleman can give the Broncos' run game a boost versus a Panthers defense allowing 140.7 rushing yards per game (third most), but I'm taking Denver because of its ability to disrupt the pocket.

Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-143): Arizona Cardinals +15 at Seattle

articles.headline: Rams' Myles Garrett on track to be activated from injured reserve, sources say
articles.description: Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett is on track to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game at the Commanders, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズのマイルズ・ギャレット、負傷者リストから復帰の見込み（関係者談）
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークが報じた関係者によると、ラムズのスターパスラッシャーであるマイルズ・ギャレットは、日曜日のコマンダーズ戦に先立ち、負傷者リストから復帰する見込みです。
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams star pass rusher Myles Garrett is on track to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game at the Washington Commanders, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Friday.

Garrett has been on injured reserve since having arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after he played in the Rams' season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

He returned to practice this week, though coach Sean McVay said Monday that he did not want to put a timeline on when Garrett would be able to play in a game.

After Week 1, Garrett had said he was not 100% healthy after dealing with knee irritation that kept him out for most of training camp.

The Rams traded for Garrett this offseason, sending two-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a first-round selection in 2027, to the Cleveland Browns. Garrett was the NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 2025 after setting the single-season sack record with 23 for the Browns.

By pairing Garrett with the unretired Aaron Donald, the Rams had hoped to have a fearsome pass rushing attack, but they rank tied for 26th in the NFL this season with 12 sacks.

articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET. We already have eight deals -- and more are on the way.

The Giants traded for Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, the Eagles sent center Cam Jurgens to the Ravens and the Texans acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. The Colts traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, too. The biggest deal yet happened on Oct. 29, with the Titans sending defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears and landing two first-round picks in return. And in the most recent trade, the Ravens got some much-needed QB help by adding Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett.

We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals will be added at the top.

Brissett's first start as the Ravens' starting quarterback could come as soon as Week 10 when Baltimore hosts the Chargers on "Monday Night Football." He was recently benched by the Cardinals before the trade.

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jacoby Brissett, Jeffery Simmons, more
articles.description: Wise move for the Ravens to add Jacoby Brissett? Did the Bears give up too much to go all-in with Jeffery Simmons? Let's evaluate eight trades before the deadline.
articles.headlineJa: NFLトレード期限の評価：ジャコビー・ブリセット、ジェフリー・シモンズらの移籍を分析
articles.descriptionJa: レイブンズによるジャコビー・ブリセットの獲得は賢明な判断だったか？ベアーズはジェフリー・シモンズに全力を注ぎすぎたのか？期限前の8つのトレードを評価します。
articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for eight deals of trading season, including two quarterback moves (Jacoby Brissett and J.J. McCarthy) and the massive blockbuster sending Jeffery Simmons to Chicago. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Jump to a trade:

Brissett | Simmons | Buckner | Nelson

Harrison | Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy

Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens

Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

Ravens grade: B+

Cardinals grade: B

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both hurt, the Ravens are throwing a Hail Mary to save their season. Baltimore is trading for veteran Brissett, shortly after the Cardinals benched him in favor of Gardner Minshew II.

Brissett is a respected bridge quarterback and has played around expectations this season in Arizona. He has a 48.9 QBR, which ranks 23rd out of 30 qualifying starters. That number alone is probably selling Brissett's performance short this season, considering he was playing behind the O-line unit that ranked 31st in pass block win rate and was able to use play-action just 18% of the time (27th-most). He has posted a plus-5% completion percentage over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats (fifth-best) along with an average 15% off-target rate. And he has been sacked 5.7% of the time (roughly average but notable, given the lack of pass protection). He did throw seven interceptions in eight games, but because he hasn't fumbled yet this season, his turnover rate is roughly average, too.

We can zoom out on Brissett's performance and see a similar picture. Since 2021, he has a 51.1 QBR and a plus-3% completion percentage over expectation (along with a 16% off-target rate), though his QBR was worse than that the past two years. All of this is to say, Brissett is rightfully a fringe starter in the NFL, but that also makes him a substantial upgrade over undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano.

The Ravens lost 33-10 to the Jaguars on Thursday night with Fagnano (and also some Derrick Henry in the wildcat) at quarterback. In all likelihood, Baltimore's season is over with Jackson currently on injured reserve and the team at 4-5. Ravens coach Jesse Minter has said Jackson's injury is "potentially" season-ending. articles.headline: Miami Heat unveil 'A Night in Vice City' jerseys ahead of GTA VI release
articles.description: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ヒート、GTA VI発売に合わせて「A Night in Vice City」ジャージを発表
articles.descriptionJa: 待ち望まれていた『グランド・セフト・オートVI』の発売日が11月19日に決定したことを受け、ヒートは発売前夜にタイムリーなリードアップイベントを開催するため、ロックスター・ゲームズと提携する。
articles.body:
The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now, but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Nov. 18 will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center.

With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.

Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings for the night. The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms, as well as "special game night activities" and "unique game night activations."

The jerseys, unveiled Friday, build on the team's past "Vice" alternates with nods to Grand Theft Auto VI and Travis Scott's Cactus Jack brand. The black Swingman jersey features pink and white accents, "Vice City" across the chest, Scott's signature flipped Nike Swoosh and a "VI" nod to the game. Six pink stars and Cactus Jack branding appear at the hem alongside a tag featuring Rockstar Games, the Heat and Cactus Jack.  Both the on-court and Swingman versions will be available in limited quantities on Nov. 18.

According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience."

The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event Thursday, lighting up "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of the Kaseya Center. The team says it will share more information about "A Night in Vice City" in the coming weeks in coordination with Rockstar Games.

The Heat's game that night against the Milwaukee Bucks will be broadcast on ESPN.

articles.headline: Dolphins to get rookie OL Kadyn Proctor back from concussion
articles.description: Dolphins left guard Kadyn Proctor has cleared concussion protocol and will play Sunday against the Lions, coach Jeff Hafley said.
articles.headlineJa: ドルフィンズ、脳震盪から復帰するルーキーOLケイディン・プロクター
articles.descriptionJa: ジェフ・ハフレイ監督は、ドルフィンズのレフトガード、ケイディン・プロクターが脳震盪プロトコルをクリアし、日曜日のライオンズ戦に出場すると発表した。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Miami Dolphins left guard Kadyn Proctor will play in Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions, coach Jeff Hafley said, after clearing concussion protocol.

Proctor displayed concussion symptoms following the Dolphins' win over the New York Jets in Week 7 and subsequently missed their loss to the New England Patriots in Week 8. He returned to the practice field Wednesday and was a full participant in each of the team's practices this week.

Hafley told reporters that the rookie officially exited the league's return to participation protocol Friday, and he was cleared for Sunday's game.

His absence was felt last week, as the Dolphins struggled to run the ball against a stout New England defense. They averaged a season-low 1.74 yards before contact per rush attempt, down from 3.09 yards before contact in their six previous games with Proctor in the lineup.

Offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik said last week was "probably our first game" where the Dolphins' blocking kept them from better production in the run game, and commended fill-in starter Jarrett Kingston for bouncing back after a slow start to the game. Running back Ollie Gordon II was also complimentary of Kingston but said the team will "get back to being us" with Proctor back in the lineup.

"When Proctor's out there, you can feel his presence out there on most every play," Slowik said. "He's just a massive guy who can move, he displaces people. He's putting defensive tackles five, six yards down the field. He caps off at the end of plays. We throw the ball 10 yards down the field for a 30-yard explosive and next thing you know, Proctor's showing up on the screen and everyone's like 'Where'd he come from.' You know what I mean?

"He just gives everybody a lot of energy when he's out there, and that's not even including what you can do with him scheme-wise."

The 6-foot-7, 360-pound Proctor was the 13th overall pick in this year's draft, and the first player taken under first-year general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan. Despite playing left tackle at Alabama, Proctor has exclusively played left guard for the Dolphins this season, where he lines up next to 6-foot-7, 325-pound left tackle Patrick Paul.

The pairing has paid off in the run game; Miami averages 6.2 yards per rush on inside runs toward the left side of the field, including 3.87 yards before first contact -- good for third-most and second-most in the NFL, respectively. The Dolphins also lead the league with 23% of their carries to that side going for 10 or more yards.

articles.headline: Chelsea's Xabi Alonso 'very happy' with Cole Palmer despite England omission
articles.description: Xabi Alonso said he has no time to spend worrying about international call-ups for his players after Cole Palmer was omitted from the England's Nations League squad.
articles.headlineJa: チェルシーのアロンソ、イングランド代表に選ばれなかったコール・パーマーに「非常に満足」
articles.descriptionJa: コール・パーマーがイングランドのネーションズリーグ代表メンバーから外れた後、シャビ・アロンソは、選手たちの代表招集について心配している時間はないと述べた。
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said he has no time to spend worrying about international call-ups for his players after Cole Palmer was omitted from the England's Nations League squad.

The 24-year-old was not amongst the 26 players named by Thomas Tuchel for the matches against Croatia and Spain, following his withdrawal from the squad during the last international break in October.

Tuchel repeated his observation that Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to stake his England claims when he discussed his latest squad on Friday.

He was not selected for the World Cup during the summer following a season that was badly hit by injuries and loss of form.

"Everything takes time but time I'm very happy with his quality and his attitude and his impact on the rest of the team."

Palmer was one of five players to withdraw from October's England squad after it had been announced.

It prompted questions around his commitment to the national team, especially since he started both matches for Chelsea either side of the international break.

Asked whether there was regret that Palmer had not made himself available, Alonso said: "We haven't talked about that. We are focused on our things, on Chelsea things, how to do better, how he can become more and more influential in games. Those are our topics.

"We speak about Chelsea. We speak about us. We have enough on our plate. We have enough to focus on each weekend."

Alonso could have goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez available to return earlier than expected for the game at the Stadium of Light, following his surgery on the fractured jaw sustained during victory at Everton last month.

- Cole Palmer 'misses too many opportunities to impress' - England boss Thomas Tuchel

- Why Cole Palmer is on notice in Tuchel's new-look England: 'The competition is on'

- Romeo Lavia: Meeting Eden Hazard gave me extra motivation to succeed at Chelsea

Should he play, the Argentina international will wear a protective mask over his face, which Alonso joked came from a specialist and "not a Halloween shop."

"[On Saturday] we have the last training session and we will decide," he said. "He's training well. Emi has made a great effort to be back. He's been ahead of the plans to be part of the team."

Moisés Caicedo will undergo a fitness test ahead of the match, although Alonso said it was not due to a recurrence of his recent calf injury.

"After the last game he had a little problem. We expect to check tomorrow. It's a discomfort more than the calf."

articles.headline: Unai Emery confirms new contract talks with Aston Villa
articles.description: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery confirmed there have been talks to build a "stronger" project at the club by signing a new contract at Villa Park.
articles.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery confirmed there have been talks to build a "stronger" project at the club by signing a new contract at Villa Park.

On Wednesday, the day after Villa's 3-0 Champions League defeat to Barcelona, the club announced they held a meeting to discuss their long-term strategy beyond 2029, when Emery's contract is due to expire.

The Villa boss has been linked with several other clubs -- including Sunday's opponents Manchester United -- but was involved with long-term talks which included the club's chairman Nassef Sawiris.

There has been no confirmation of a new deal for the Spaniard, but Emery touched on committing his long-term future with the club and says there will be further contract talks next week.

He said: "My ambition is to keep our consistency and how we are improving and building lots of things positively. It is a huge challenge.

"They decided, speaking with us last year, to build a new stand to add more supporters at Villa Park. That is a clear step forward to get better.

"How we are increasing our budget each year, and revenue through our performance by playing in Europe and improving players, selling players, then buying young talented players, this is the process and ambition we should keep in the future.

"I had a good meeting with Nassef Sawiris, very good meeting, very positive. Let's talk next week, trying to get everything we spoke about together.

"We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a deal, yes."

Villa will be looking to extend their five-match unbeaten run when they face Manchester United on Sunday who have won only one of their opening nine league matches -- beating Ipswich in August.

Old Trafford has not been a happy hunting ground for Villa in recent years and they have lost each of their last six matches there in all competitions.

Emery is not underestimating Michael Carrick's side and even described them as being at the same level as Spanish giants Barcelona.

"We did not win one match there in four years," he added.

"We lost to Barcelona because of the level we faced; this is the highest level in the Champions League. Man United is at the same level as Barcelona.

"I am very demanding. The next challenge on Sunday is in the process we have and trying to do better than we did against Barcelona on Tuesday."

Villa were beaten for the first time in this season's Champions League on Tuesday courtesy of Lamine Yamal's opener and Raphinha's double.

articles.headline: Doc Rivers: Giannis 'didn't want to be the bad guy' when seeking Bucks exit
articles.description: Former Bucks coach Doc Rivers said Giannis Antetokounmpo "didn't want to be the bad guy" when he was trying to seek a trade out of Milwaukee last season.
articles.body:
Former Milwaukee Bucks coach Doc Rivers said Giannis Antetokounmpo kept "yo-yoing" by not publicly requesting a trade before ultimately being dealt to the Miami Heat this summer.

"Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn't want to be the bad guy," Rivers told "The Bill Simmons Podcast" in an episode posted Thursday. "He wanted [GM Jon Horst and owner Wes Edens] and those guys to say, 'We're trading you,' instead of him asking for a trade. To me, that was the game that was being played."

The 2025-26 season for the Bucks was largely overshadowed by the question of Antetokounmpo's future with the franchise he led to the 2021 NBA championship. Throughout the season, Antetokounmpo told multiple outlets, including ESPN, that he was committed to the Bucks and would "never" demand a trade.

However, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that Antetokounmpo and his agent, Alex Saratsis, had consistently informed the Bucks since May 2025 that he wanted a trade and believed it was best for both sides to part ways. That ended with the Bucks trading Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, one pick swap and one second-round pick.

The Heat are off to a slow start in Antetokounmpo's first season, going 3-6 through Thursday's 120-100 loss to the Golden State Warriors. Antetokounmpo is leading the Heat in points (27.3 PPG) and rebounding (12.7 RPG).

Rivers discussed the challenges of coaching Antetokounmpo, telling Simmons he wished that Antetokounmpo had stepped up as more of a leader in Milwaukee.

"Giannis needed to just give himself to the team, not to anyone else," Rivers said.

He also addressed Antetokounmpo's style of play as a unique problem.

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers told Simmons. "He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

"I wish he learned how to execute better," Rivers added. "He's one of those guys ... that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shootarounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach [Erik Spoelstra] who is as good as there is in execution."

Rivers coached the Bucks for three seasons, going 97-103 with two first-round playoff exits before Milwaukee missed the postseason entirely last season for the first time since 2015-16. The day after the 2025-26 regular-season finale, the Bucks announced that Rivers would not return as coach.

articles.headline: Arsenal's Mikel Arteta praises Declan Rice's 'desperate' determination to improve
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has lauded Declan Rice's "desperate" determination to improve after the midfielder was one of five Arsenal players called up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has lauded Declan Rice's "desperate" determination to improve after the midfielder was one of five Arsenal players called up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.

Rice has contributed five Premier League assists this season -- the most of any player in the competition -- as well as a Champions League goal, in 14 appearances across all competitions.

The Arsenal boss also praised the mindset of Noni Madueke, who was not among the England boss' selections, and believes he will use his omission as fuel.

Asked what has changed in Rice's performance, Arteta said: "The mentality to go out and win football matches and to add another level to his game, another kind of threat and be much more unpredictable, and we've been working a lot on that.

"He's desperate to improve every part of his game, and we need to do that while we maintain so many incredible things that he's already done, but he's on the right trajectory."

Arteta agreed Rice had also strengthened his ball progression, and explained his thinking behind dropping the 27-year-old deeper.

"I think we cannot restrict his qualities and his capacities," Arteta said. "He can drop back, he can progress play. He can drop back, he can carry the ball, he can be incredible in transition.

- England squad for Nations League: Jobe Bellingham selected, Cole Palmer left out

- Ronaldo's Portugal career ended in shame, but at his peak he was a dominant force

"He can win duels. He can produce passes by arriving, by playing far, by crossing the ball left or right, it doesn't matter. On set pieces [too], he's got a lot to offer. His shooting ability from long range as well is something that we need to use more. He has the capacity to do it. So, continue to go to play because there's still so much to gain."

Rice is rumoured to be close to signing a new deal, but Arteta revealed he does not look too far ahead when it comes to conversations with Rice about how he envisions his role on the pitch years down the line.

He said: "We haven't been that far yet. Obviously, we have still a lot to do. A period of a season, I think it's enough. There are other things that are part of his role in the team, like the club, which I think they can envision with a bit more time. But what his performance was and impact on the team, I think it has to be short-term."

Rice joins Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Eberechi Eze in the England camp, while Madueke misses out.

"I leave that to Thomas," Arteta said. "There were so many options, he needs to make decisions, he's made that one this time and that's it, I leave that completely to him."

Arteta was delighted by Madueke's mentality last international break, when he was also left out of Tuchel's squad.

"What he did is he went abroad and he trained," said Arteta. "That's Noni, and that's his mindset. He wants to get better."

articles.body:
Right around this time every year, you can start to feel it. The air gets a little crisper. The shadows get a little colder. The days get shorter. The tree colors start to pop. You start wearing sweaters. Pumpkins appear in places where they do and do not belong.

Everyone and everything starts to shift, just slightly, in preparation for what's about to happen. The cycles of nature can be fickle and unpredictable, so the date is never exactly the same, and some years come and go without anything at all. But most years, it does.

Our tiny little rituals prime us to anticipate the inevitable, oncoming shift: that moment when Manchester United fire their manager and convince themselves that the new guy is finally going to be the one who fixes everything.

Ruben Amorim lost his job last January. Erik ten Hag was fired two years ago, right before Halloween. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer got the boot just a couple days before Thanksgiving. And Jose Mourinho was relieved of his duties a little over a week before Christmas.

Now that we've once again entered the season of sacking, Michael Carrick seems like he will inevitably become the latest victim.

Man United are clear of the relegation zone on goal differential alone. If history is any indication, their comeback against AS Roma in the Champions League will end up being meaningless. Before Tuesday's win, Carrick appeared to be on the verge of tears at the end of every match.

This is the 14th season since Manchester United last won the Premier League. And whoever replaces Carrick will be the ninth coach to try and do something that no other United manager since has done: just, simply, meet the expectations at one of the richest sports teams on the planet for more than a single season in a row.

But given how many different coaches have now failed since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club, it makes you wonder: Could anyone have been successful at Manchester United?

What is a great manager worth?

Arsenal won the Premier League last season with 85 points.

If we lived in a world where there were no subs and everyone on the field contributed exactly evenly to their team's success, then all 11 Arsenal players would have contributed about 8 points (7.7, to be slightly more exact) of value last season.

Except, the alternative to each player isn't just zero points. If you removed Bukayo Saka from the lineup, you wouldn't have to play a man down. No, you'd get to put another player out there who would also contribute to winning to some degree.

So, let's look at the relegation-level cut-off. West Ham were relegated with 39 points. Using the same framework, we'd say that all of their players were worth a little over 3.5 points across the season. We could then say that the average Arsenal player provided 5 more points of value than a relegation-level player.
